title: Kling AI Experiment: Avatar Transitions and Realism
content:
# ✨️**Exploring _Kling AI_ for Enhanced Avatar Renders and Transitions✨️**

Hi everyone!  
In this post, I’d like to share a recent experiment where I used **Kling AI** to enhance the realism of my avatar renders and create smoother transitions between poses.

![cea42fee163a484c9257fb551def7258](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/20d2fae3d9e64e1ba1e875849b4a8483/images/cea42fee163a484c9257fb551def7258YouCut_20250612_071032878-ezgif.com-video-to-webp-converter-2.webp)

* * *

For this project, I used 3 different renders.

![d175ff247f9f46fe87280d0185da57f9](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/20d2fae3d9e64e1ba1e875849b4a8483/images/d175ff247f9f46fe87280d0185da57f951-2-1.JPG)

I used two of them — one as the starting frame and one as the ending frame — to showcase a transformation. Then, I used the **YouCut** app simply to stitch the two short video clips together, creating a seamless visual flow.

![ea2ea68c3b734cfbb16aebf5ca8a6d0c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/20d2fae3d9e64e1ba1e875849b4a8483/images/ea2ea68c3b734cfbb16aebf5ca8a6d0cScreenshot_20250612-082640_Gallery.jpg)

The results were quite promising. Kling AI added a dynamic and lifelike quality to the avatars that made the scene feel more animated and expressive.

* * *

While the results were quite promising in some cases, I also had several failed attempts. For example, in some of the test videos below, the outputs didn’t turn out well due to unclear camera angles, using only a single reference image, overly long or vague prompts, or excessive avatar motion. These factors often led to unnatural or broken animations.

![c726f1eb9a4f42f5b6823f48f3cd5b21](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/20d2fae3d9e64e1ba1e875849b4a8483/images/c726f1eb9a4f42f5b6823f48f3cd5b2120250612_060527613-ezgif.com-video-to-webp-converter.webp)![8847a312affd4c4cb8faef2939b1bd67](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/20d2fae3d9e64e1ba1e875849b4a8483/images/8847a312affd4c4cb8faef2939b1bd6720250612_061319862-ezgif.com-video-to-webp-converter.webp)![aa2b66361244460f916ecf083224f08f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/20d2fae3d9e64e1ba1e875849b4a8483/images/aa2b66361244460f916ecf083224f08f20250612_061311259-ezgif.com-video-to-webp-converter.webp)

Still, it's been a valuable learning process — and I'm excited to keep experimenting and refining the workflow!

* * *

[_https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/cfd99926816a4eb7bcbd6dd816c2f841_](https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/cfd99926816a4eb7bcbd6dd816c2f841)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/20d2fae3d9e64e1ba1e875849b4a8483/images/4a5b490ba544416ea0b9806696cb119e50-3.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/20d2fae3d9e64e1ba1e875849b4a8483/images/49d159017edd4ad3b7cce2bfd65c00ca50-3.png)

title: Ambient Occlusion bake appears too dark with thick export
content:
Does anyone experience an issue when exporting from Marvelous Designer to Substance Painter using the **Thick** option, where the Ambient Occlusion bake appears too dark or black around areas like attached pockets or additional fabric layers? How can this be fixed?![397d015345a6476699b29fba481c3b9d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/7e701247ab4d49f5b6cf3247fc8f275a/images/397d015345a6476699b29fba481c3b9dimage_2025-06-09_171540189.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: I asked ChatGPT and it replied:When exporting with "Thick" option:MD creates two-sided geometry (inner and outer surface), resulting in very tight gaps between fabric layers.These narrow spaces cause ray occlusion artifacts during AO baking — rays bounce between the tight layers, resulting in overly dark shadows.In overlapping parts like pockets, this is amplified because the geometry is even closer.
Reply 1: ✅ Solutions and Workarounds: 1. Use "Thin" Export and Add Thickness in Painter or Later Best Practice: Export with the "Thin" option from MD, and add thickness as a normal map or displacement in Painter or during rendering.Why? This avoids problematic geometry and gives clean bakes. 2. Adjust AO Baking Settings in Substance Painter If you must use thick geometry: In the Bake Mesh Maps window, tweak:Max Frontal Distance: Increase it slightly (e.g., from 0.01 to 0.03).Max Rear Distance: Lower it or tweak based on your mesh.Self Occlusion: Try changing from Always to By Mesh Name.Use Cage: Use a custom cage mesh if you have one to better control ray directions. 3. Manually Clean AO Map After baking, you can paint out or soften overly dark AO areas directly in Painter’s 2D view using a paint layer and AO as a mask or fill. 4. Rework Pocket Geometry in MD If the pocket is too flush with the base garment, increase the offset (e.g., pull the pocket out by 1–2 mm more).You can also freeze and simulate with more distance to force a gap. 5. Use Mesh Naming Conventions for Baking Name overlapping parts distinctly (e.g., Body_Shirt, Pocket_Left) and use "Match by Name" baking in Painter. This reduces baking artifacts between intersecting pieces.

Comment 2: Hello, you can usually check if the side of the normals is correct. If it is still failing, you may take it to a photo editor like Photoshop and invert those areas that you believe remain dark, because the program recognized that they are "flipped".
Reply 1: Thanks for the suggestion! I checked, and the normals are correct especially when I export using the Thin option. The dark areas mostly appear only on parts where I added rendering thickness to the fabric in Marvelous Designer, like pockets and layered elements. That seems to be what's causing the issue during the AO bake in Substance Painter.
content_description: This webpage aims to provide solutions and troubleshooting tips for users experiencing overly dark or black Ambient Occlusion bakes when exporting from Marvelous Designer to Substance Painter with the Thick option.
